clue.text: Husband in a jam

definitions.meaning: to husband is to use sparingly, keep back for later
a preserve of fruit boiled with sugar

explanation.surface: A married man finds himself in a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the idea of preserving: to save resources carefully, and fruit preserved in sugar.

clue.text: Our Carla may be forecasting the future

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters of the name could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman named Carla tries her hand at fortune-telling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' signals the anagram of OUR CARLA, giving the eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Oracular describes the prophetic speech of an oracle, who foretells what is to come.

clue.text: Picture for personal interest only

parts.note: a painting whose sole subject is the painter's own person, so it is literally of personal interest

explanation.surface: A photo kept just for one's own private enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting of the artist by the artist concerns only that person.

clue.text: Tell us again about the turf

parts.note: re means about, concerning
peat is turf cut from a bog for fuel

explanation.surface: A request to hear once more the tale of the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: To say something a second time is to reiterate it.

clue.text: Memorable part of a movie picture

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A scene from a film that sticks in the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something epic is grand and heroic, hence worth remembering.

clue.text: Cooked apricot left in a very warm place

indicators.note: cooked suggests the fruit is reworked and altered, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stewed fruit forgotten somewhere hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' is the anagram signal; the definition is a phrase describing location, as in plants grown in hot regions.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropical means situated in the tropics, the hot region near the equator.

clue.text: Is in reverse unless it's in Latin

indicators.note: in reverse says the two short words before it are read backwards as one run

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grammar note about a Latin conjunction meaning unless.
explanation.walkthrough: IS IN read backwards gives the answer; 'in' is fodder, 'reverse' the indicator. A decree nisi is a divorce order that takes effect unless cause is shown.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word nisi translates as unless, familiar from the legal decree nisi.

clue.text: Near fortune acquired accidentally

parts.note: by means near, beside
chance is luck or fortune

explanation.surface: Wealth gained without anyone intending it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening by chance happens without design, by accident.

clue.text: Shame about the gold: very large size but in a state full of holes

indicators.note: about means the word for shame wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: it's a pity means it's a shame
or is gold in heraldry
OS stands for outsize, a very large clothing size

explanation.surface: A lament about gold and oversized goods, ending in a riddled condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal, so the word for shame wraps both short pieces; OS (outsize) is a clothing-label abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Porosity is the quality of being porous, having many tiny openings.

clue.text: Flag I found in the river

indicators.note: found in says the single letter is placed within the river's name

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall

explanation.surface: A banner discovered floating in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The FAL is a short river in Cornwall, south-west England; 'found in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to weaken or tire, which is to falter or not succeed.

clue.text: Shine in two languages

parts.note: French is one language
Polish is another language

explanation.surface: Someone who excels in a pair of foreign tongues.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a high-gloss finish rubbed onto fine wooden furniture with shellac.

clue.text: A beer and a gin perhaps give us the gist

definitions.text: A beer and a gin perhaps
definitions.meaning: a beer is a long drink and a gin a short one
the essential point, as in the phrase of it

explanation.surface: Ordering a couple of drinks while asking for the main point.
explanation.definitionFit: Pub terms divide drinks into long and short; the idiom of it means the essential summary.

clue.text: Distributed everything to back young Edward

parts.note: all means everything

indicators.note: back says the little word to is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: Ted is a familiar short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Giving all one has in support of a boy called Ted.
explanation.definitionFit: Allotted means shared out or apportioned, as rations are handed round.

clue.text: Fear has gone right in

indicators.note: in says the letter for right is placed within the other word

parts.note: someone who has gone has died, so is dead

explanation.surface: Fear has entered someone's mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great apprehension or terror.

clue.text: Make a record of that Scottish ravine

parts.note: to can a performance is to record it, as in having it in the can
yon is a Scots word for that

explanation.surface: Recording the sound of a Highland gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: In film and music, a finished recording is 'in the can'.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep, narrow valley cut by a river, a gorge.

clue.text: The quiet deserter is a bit of an ass

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
a rat is someone who deserts, as rats leave a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A silent defector is rather foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on two senses: a fool, and the buttocks (British slang).
explanation.definitionFit: Prat is British slang for a fool, and also, archaically, for the buttocks, literally part of one's backside.

clue.text: Quietly, though heavily moves in following the men who fix the pipes

definitions.text: the men who fix the pipes

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
to lumber is to move heavily and clumsily

explanation.surface: Tradesmen trudging in softly after someone.
explanation.definitionFit: These tradespeople install and repair water pipes and drains.

clue.text: Thought the student was perfect

parts.note: an idea is a thought
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A notion that the pupil was flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner from the L-plates on British learner drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means flawless, exactly as one would wish.

clue.text: The new resident was put in

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of the word are made fresh by rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone who has just moved into the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Inserted means placed into something.

clue.text: Spots a hundred points

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
N and E are compass points, north and east

explanation.surface: A score of a hundred on a scoreboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition marked by pimples.

clue.text: Menu changed around midday to something completely unknown

indicators.note: around means the word for midday wraps around the jumbled letters

parts.note: noon is midday

indicators.note: changed says the letters of the word menu are altered in order

explanation.surface: A lunchtime menu revised into a mystery dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' scrambles the menu and 'around' wraps midday about it; the definition is a philosophical term, which makes the clue feel obscure.
explanation.definitionFit: In Kant's philosophy, a noumenon is a thing in itself, beyond perception and so unknowable.

clue.text: High class ships move below the surface perhaps

definitions.text: High class ships move below the surface perhaps

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U speech
boats are ships

explanation.surface: Smart vessels that might travel underwater.
explanation.walkthrough: U as upper-class comes from 1950s British usage, U and non-U.
explanation.definitionFit: These were German submarines, warships that operate under water.

clue.text: Almost full after 14-very nasty!

indicators.note: after says the trimmed word comes behind the other piece

parts.note: the answer to 14 down, a word for fear

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is dropped from the word

explanation.surface: An exclamation of disgust at something horrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last L of FULL; 'after' puts it behind the answer to 14 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadful means awful or extremely bad.

clue.text: Persuade another ten to decorate the cake

indicators.note: another suggests a different version of the word, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: to ice a cake is to cover it with icing

explanation.surface: Urging ten more people to help with cake decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to lure or tempt someone into acting.

clue.text: Sweet goat takes whisky

parts.note: a goat is a butter, an animal that butts
Scotch is whisky from Scotland

explanation.surface: A goat helping itself to a dram.
explanation.walkthrough: The pun: a goat butts, so it is a 'butter'; the surface makes it a creature sipping a dram.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterscotch is a hard toffee-like confection made from brown sugar and butter.

clue.text: Small group involved in riot

indicators.note: involved in suggests the letters are tangled up together, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A handful of people caught up in a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' signals the anagram of RIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a set of three, a little band or party.

clue.text: Curtails the short routes

definitions.meaning: short ___ are quicker ways to a place

explanation.surface: Reducing the length of the quicker paths.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means trims or reduces, and also the second half of shortcuts, the quicker routes.

clue.text: Confesses to crushing snow

indicators.note: crushing suggests the word is squashed and broken up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Admitting to trampling on the snow.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up, or own to something, is to admit it.

clue.text: Put money in again to get clothing following restraint

indicators.note: following says the clothing piece comes after the restraint

parts.note: a rein is a restraint, as on a horse
a vest is an item of clothing

explanation.surface: Advice on putting funds back in after holding back on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinvest is to put returns back into an investment.

clue.text: See night falling like a broad expanse of cloth

indicators.note: falling suggests the words tumble apart, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Watching night descend as if a vast blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling' signals the anagram of SEE NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheeting is fabric made for bed linen, or any wide spread of material.
